title: Platform systems & services: central playbook, dashboards, runbooks, and Q2 2026 roadmap (v2)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates platform systems and services guidance: production dashboards, alerting rules, runbooks for common incidents, day-to-day operational how-tos, a short retrospective for Q1 2026, and the team roadmap for Q2 2026. It is intended as the single reference for the Platform Engineering team (hands-on SREs, platform engineers, and oncall responders).

Key objectives
- Provide a consistent incident response experience across services (API gateway, router, autoscaler, KV cache, model-serving pool).
- Maintain actionable dashboards and SLOs to detect regressions early.
- Provide clear runbooks and escalation paths to reduce MTTR.
- Capture short term roadmap and owners for Q2 2026.

Ownership and contacts
- Platform Systems & Services (primary): eng-platform
  - Primary owner: Asha Patel (platform-systems)
  - Secondary owner: Diego Morales (observability)
- Oncall escalation chain (24x7):
  1. Primary oncall (Platform): PagerDuty schedule: platform-primary
  2. Secondary oncall (Eng-SRE): PagerDuty schedule: platform-secondary
  3. Engineering manager oncall: Linnea Berg (Slack @LinneaB)

SLOs and key metrics
- Global API request latency (p50/p95/p99): target p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms.
- Error rate (5m rolling): target < 0.5% for 99.9% of time.
- Router request success rate: 99.95% monthly.
- Autoscaler convergence time: target < 60s for scale up to sustain 95th percentile traffic bursts.

Dashboards (Grafana)
- Dashboard: Platform Overview (dash-id: platform_overview) — high level KPIs
  - Panels: global QPS, 1m/5m error rate, tail latency heatmap, active model shards, GPU utilization by cluster.
- Dashboard: Router & Gateway (dash-id: router_gateway)
  - Panels: request count per route, 4xx/5xx breakdown, backend latency per model variant, prefix cache hit rate.
- Dashboard: Serving Pools (dash-id: serving_pools)
  - Panels: per-pool utilization, queue depth, concurrency per worker, avg tokens/sec.
- Dashboard: Autoscaler (dash-id: autoscaler)
  - Panels: desired vs actual replicas, scale events timeline, CPU/GPU headroom, scaling errors.

Suggested Grafana panels and alert thresholds
| Panel | Metric | Alert threshold (5m) | Severity |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Global p95 latency | request_latency_ms{quantile="0.95"} | > 120 | P2 |
| Global p99 latency | request_latency_ms{quantile="0.99"} | > 300 | P1 |
| Error rate | sum(increase(request_errors_total[5m]))/sum(increase(request_total[5m])) | > 0.01 (1%) | P1 |
| Router 5xx rate | increase(router_5xx_total[5m]) | > 5/min | P1 |
| KV cache hit rate | rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]) | < 0.70 | P2 |

Alerting rules (Prometheus-style examples)
- High error rate (P1)
  expr: sum(increase(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(increase(request_total[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels: severity=P1, team=platform
  annotations: runbook: /confluence/platform/runbooks/high-error-rate

- p99 latency breach (P1)
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 0.3
  for: 5m
  labels: severity=P1, team=platform

Runbooks (top incidents)
1) High global error rate (P1)
  - Symptoms: sudden spike in 5xx across multiple routes, user reports of failures, increased retries in client logs.
  - Immediate actions (first 10 minutes):
    1. Triage: confirm signal on Platform Overview and Router dashboard. Note scope (all routes or specific models).
    2. Run quick queries: top 10 routes by 5xx in last 5m, check recent deploys (platformctl list-deploys --since 30m).
    3. If scoped to a single service, page that service owner and revert the last canary (platformctl rollback --service <svc> --to-last-stable).
    4. If global, enable degraded mode: route traffic to fallback model variant (routing policy: fallback=fast-small) and open incident channel.
  - Postmortem checklist: collect request traces, core logs, deployment timeline, and create Incident Review.

2) Serving pool saturation (P1/P2)
  - Symptoms: queue growth, autoscaler failing to provision new nodes, GPU OOM errors.
  - Immediate actions:
    1. Check Serving Pools dashboard for queue depth and worker OOMs.
    2. Manually scale pool as temporary mitigation: platformctl scale-pool --pool <name> --replicas <n>.
    3. If autoscaler errors present, check autoscaler logs (/var/log/autoscaler/*.log) and restart service: systemctl restart platform-autoscaler on control plane host.
    4. If GPU OOMs persist, reduce max tokens or evict large requests via rate limit policy.

3) Loss of metrics / alerting (P1)
  - Symptoms: no data in Grafana, Prometheus targets down.
  - Immediate actions:
    1. Check Prometheus status and target list (prometheus:9090/targets).
    2. If Prometheus is down, SSH to monitoring leader and inspect systemd logs: journalctl -u prometheus -n 200.
    3. If long-term data missing, follow monitoring runbook to restore from longterm remote_write or standby Prometheus.

How-tos and operational primitives
- Adding a panel to the Platform Overview dashboard
  1. Fork the dashboard JSON from Grafana repo: infra/grafana/dashboards/platform_overview.json.
  2. Add panel with consistent naming and panel id. Run grafcli apply --file platform_overview.json --env prod.
  3. Notify #platform-dashboards with a short summary and link to PR.

- Oncall playbook for night shift
  1. Check Platform Overview and Router dashboards on start of shift.
  2. Acknowledge and triage any firing alerts; set incident priority and create an incident channel with template: incident:create --type platform --priority P1.
  3. Keep notes in the incident log and update the incident channel with mitigation steps.

Runbook templates and artifacts
- Incident doc template: include summary, timeline, mitigation, root cause, contributing factors, action items, and owners.
- Postmortem cadence: all P1 incidents require a postmortem within 72 hours and assigned owner for follow ups.

Q1 2026 retrospective (high level)
- Wins:
  - Reduced average p95 latency by 18% through kernel selection improvements and cache warming.
  - Improved autoscaler reliability after introducing prewarm scheduling; scale convergence latency down to median 42s.
- Areas for improvement:
  - Several incidents traced to runaway prompt amplification; we will add automated throttling for long-running sessions.
  - Dashboards lacked a unified error taxonomy; we will standardize 4xx/5xx tagging and add route-level error breakdowns.
  - Documentation gaps in playbooks for private deployments surfaced during onprem rollout.

Action items from retro (owner / target)
- Standardize error tags across services — Diego Morales — 2026-04-30
- Implement request throttling for long sessions — Samir Gupta — 2026-05-15
- Consolidate dashboards and add route-level error panels — Linnea Berg — 2026-05-01

Roadmap: Q2 2026 (high level)
- M1: Unified observability workstream (owner: Diego Morales) — goals:
  - Merge per-service dashboards into Platform Overview and add SLO burn rate panels.
  - Add synthetic traffic jobs for critical routes (canary latency checks).
- M2: Autoscaler hardening (owner: Asha Patel) — goals:
  - Add preemptible GPU handling, improve backoff logic, succeed rate target 99.9%.
  - Add blue/green scaling test harness in staging.
- M3: Runbook automation (owner: Samir Gupta) — goals:
  - Implement one-click rollback and routing overrides via the platformctl UI.
  - Integrate runbooks with PagerDuty annotations so alerts include runbook links.
- M4: Team wiki and onboarding (owner: Linnea Berg) — goals:
  - Publish curated oncall checklist and 90-day onboarding for new platform engineers.
  - Run two game days focusing on serving pool saturation and Prometheus failover.

Quarter milestones and acceptance criteria
- End of May: Platform Overview dashboards merged, synthetic canaries running for top 10 routes.
- End of June: Autoscaler blue/green tests in staging and failure modes documented; rollback automation available in prod (feature-flagged).
